chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me, saying: Abu al-Husayn al-Abbas ibn al-Mughairah narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Marwan ibn Uthman, who said:

When the people swore allegiance to Abu Bakr, Ali (peace be upon him), al-Zubair, and al-Miqdad entered the house of Fatimah (peace be upon her) and refused to come out. So Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Set the house on fire upon them." Then al-Zubair came out with his sword. So Abu Bakr said: "Seize the dog." They advanced toward him, but he slipped and fell to the ground, and the sword fell from his hand. Then Abu Bakr said: "Strike it against the stone." So his sword was struck against the stone until it broke.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) left toward al-Aliyah, and Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas met him. He said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu al-Hasan?" He said: "They wanted to burn down my house, while Abu Bakr sits on the pulpit receiving allegiance, neither preventing that nor condemning it." Thabit said to him: "My palm shall not leave your hand until I am killed defending you." So they both went together until they returned to Madinah.

And there was Fatimah (peace be upon her) standing at her door, and her house had been emptied of all the people, and she was saying: "I have never known an assembly of people worse than you. You left the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace) as a corpse before us, and you resolved your affairs among yourselves without seeking our counsel, and you did to us what you did, and you recognized no right for us."

key_terms.العالية: Al-Aliyah - the upper quarter of Madinah
key_terms.بيعة: Bay'ah - oath of allegiance to a political leader

ai.seo_question: What happened at the house of Fatimah after the Prophet Muhammad's death according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of al-Mufid describes the events immediately following the Prophet Muhammad's death, when some companions refused to accept the caliphate of Abu Bakr. Ali, al-Zubair, and al-Miqdad took refuge in the house of Fatimah, and Umar threatened to burn the house. The narrative culminates in Fatimah's passionate rebuke of the community for abandoning the Prophet's body while seizing power and denying the rights of the Prophet's family.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported to me from Abu al-Husayn al-Abbas ibn al-Mughairah, who reported from Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Mansoor al-Ramadi, who reported from Saeed ibn Ufayr who reported from Ibn Lah’eah, from Khalid ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Marwan ibn Uthman who said:

When people swore the allegiance on the hands of Abu Bakr, ‘Ali (as), al-Zubair and al-Miqdad entered the house of Fatimah, peace be upon her, and refused to come out. So, Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Set the house on fire upon them." Then al-Zubair came out with his sword. So Abu Bakr said: "Catch this dog." As they advanced towards him, he (al-Zubair) slipped and fell and the sword fell off his hand. Then Abu Bakr said: "Hit him with the stone." Zubair hit the stone till it broke.

‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) left the house from the direction of Aaliyah and met Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. He said: "O Abul Hasan, what has happened to you?" He said: "They have resolved on burning down my house, while Abu Bakr is sitting on the pulpit, receiving allegiance, he neither prevents them for doing it nor is he condemning it." Thabit said: "My palm will not leave your hand, till I am killed by your side." So they moved forward together till they came back towards Madinah

while Fatimah (peace be upon her) stood at her door, and all of the people had left her house. She was saying: "I have not known of an assembly of people worse than you; you left the messenger of Allah unattended, when his corpse lay before us; you resolved about your affairs among yourselves, refusing to seek our leadership; and you did to us what you did, and you recognized no right for us."
